item.title: Why it'd be bad to remove gravity:
item.content:encoded:
1. Black holes disappear.
2. Satellites basically stop working.
3. Solar systems stop working.
4. Suns asplode.
5. I don't think galaxies work anymore either.
6. In general, universe as we know it fucking dies.
I propose it to be possible instead to adjust your own personal gravity. Imagine the possibilities…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Actually, it was a debate about whether gravity SHOULD exist. SCP-946-1 was leading the debate and SCP-946-2 was not giving much resistance. When the researcher joined the debate, he persuaded 946-2 to his side of the argument (that side being that gravity should exist). If SCP-946-2 HAD given up, the researcher would not have time to have joined and suddenly the universe would be without a key physical principal. The debater's job isn't to fix the universe, it is to preserve the universe.
Also, the single light source requirement was not always in place. The photo is likely from before 946-1 and -2 decided that a single light improved the atmosphere.

I GET IT NOW.
They were having a debate about gravity and whether it exists or not, and of course it wouldn't be euclid in the first place if their debates didn't have an effect on the universe, so when SCP-942-2 gave up, the opposing side changed the universe to make gravity real, and that fucked everything up, because gravity actually ISN'T how SCP-942-1 and the debating researcher perceived it to be. The entire universe did something extremely odd and the researcher was able to turn the argument over before any extreme damage was done. This is why a skilled debater must be present at all times. If one of them screws up the laws of physics, there has to be a debater around to convince them otherwise, and return things to normal.
Thus making this SCP extremely dangerous and hard to contain. Thus making it Keter.

Also, I don't like the white background in the photo. If it says a single light source should be directly above SCP-942 at all times, it should show that in the photo.

item.title: The real reason SCP-946 should be Keter
item.content:encoded:
Incident 946-██

Date: ██/██/1994 - SCP-946-1 and SCP-946-2 began to debate the merits and value of “Special Edition” films. SCP-946-1 argued that a movie was the property of the original creator, and if that person wanted to modify or alter their film, it was their right to do so, and they can and should call their new version the “correct” version.

SCP-946-2 argued that film is a “collective experience” and that after it has been watched and has become beloved by millions of individuals, making major changes to the film’s theme or storyline (and proceeding to tell those people that the version they fell in love with is not the “real one”) tarnishes the experience and the memory, diminishing the value of the original film.

Their discussion continued for many hours, but eventually SCP-946-2 conceded the argument, and SCP-946-1 stated, “So, George gets to do it.”

They then disappeared.

(Just meant as a joke, honest!)

Given the abilities of SCP-946-a and SCP-946-b, it seems implausible that blowing up the table would be at all helpful.

The likely result is that they pick a new table: and may then decide they don't like the Foundation any more.

Backup explosives I can see as a last-ditch option, but I don't think they'd be mentioned in the standard containment procedures listing: You can't use D-class for the debating and if you tell the researchers "If you don't argue well enough we'll blow you up" that'll make them less eager to step into the debates at all.
The only problem: The moment you set hidden explosives, SCP-946-a and SCP-946-b will be aware of it.

That's… not crazy. If there is no reason to assume something, you don't. If they don't have a reason to doubt the possible efficacy of explosives as a last-ditch effort, then they wouldn't. Even if they were unsure, it beats the hell out of every star in the universe spontaneously going nova, the rotational force of every spheroid body ripping it apart, galaxies flying apart, etc.

Things like this are, I would argue, case in point why the Foundation can't afford to be slow to react and handle everything like a hideously convoluted bureaucracy. They fuck this up and everything dies, and the same can be said of a lot of things under their charge. It would take a few people trained with explosives a matter of minutes to rig everything in the room, which I would expect to be ordered by the site directors pretty quickly once the seriousness of the threat this posed became evident.

item.content:encoded: Aha. Allow me to explain, then. Now, let's say this just happened. The Foundation has had this major incident. In response to this incident, the containment procedures were altered to their current state. But the Foundation is nothing if not a bureaucracy. It would probably take a while for them to sort out some better methods than "talk them down". How does one go about destroying them? Have they concluded a debate in the past making themselves invulnerable? Will destroying them have catastrophic consequences? The Foundation has a lot of things to sort out before they go doing crazy things with the procedures.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Sorts argued thusly:

Right now, in the time frame captured by the document, they have an unusual but pretty civil SCP item. It summons guys and they discuss things. There are sometimes anomalous results but no one really thought these guys were going to argue reality out of existence.

Except they did almost do it, and, as the article clearly states in Addendum 2:

SCP-946-2 agreed with Dr ███████, who continued to argue with SCP-946-1 for nearly two hours, before, frustrated, SCP-946-1 gave up. Containment procedures updated in light of this event. Object Class upgrade to Keter pending approval.

And, as I originally stated:

I find it somewhat hard to believe that the Foundation's single precautionary measure against allowing these people to potentially destroy the entire universe amounts to, "Try to talk them down and hope for the best." … I think they would at least rig the table/chairs/room with explosives in case it looks like they won't be talked down.

Because there is no mention of any additional precautionary measures (despite Addendum 2 saying the containment procedures had been updated) save trying to talk these people down, and that is quite simply leaving the fate of the entire world in the hands of an individual's debating abilities with no backup plan whatsoever when, if there was one, it ought to be outlined there.

Make sense?
